sources.title: Introducing Muse Spark 1.1
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. July 9 launch identifies exact Muse Spark 1.1 and its coding, computer-use and multi-agent training; it publishes no nominal total or active parameter count.

sources.title: Models - Meta Model API
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Lists exact 1.1 with 1,048,576-token context and text/image/video/audio/PDF inputs. Three hosted Spark versions share modalities and context; the separate Open section publishes 816B total and 42B active. The shared capabilities alone are not the basis for the parameter inference.

sources.title: Muse Spark 1.1 Evaluation Report
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 and searched the complete 112-page report. It identifies 1.1 as the July 9 update to Muse Spark 1.0 and documents developer-controlled tool/function calling, but does not directly state total or active parameter counts or a production architecture.

sources.title: Meta Model API Terms of Service
sources.evidence: October 9, 2026 terms reserve ownership of Services to Meta/licensors and restrict extracting weights or deriving proprietary components. API access is governed by these terms separately from any open-weight license.

sources.title: Meta Model API Model Designation and Geographic Use Policy
sources.evidence: October 12, 2026 policy explicitly designates Muse Spark 1.1 a Standard Model under the API Terms; Contributor designations apply to 1.2 and 1.3 variants.

sources.title: Reasoning - Meta Model API
sources.evidence: Spark models generate internal reasoning tokens before output. Reasoning effort is configurable; max is specifically limited to newer supported models, so it is not inferred for 1.1.

sources.title: Muse Spark 1.2 & Muse Code Evaluation Methodology
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Exact 1.1 is a comparator at xhigh reasoning effort; the complete three-page methodology contains no parameter or activated-parameter comparison column.

sources.title: Muse Spark 1.3 Evaluation Report
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 and searched the complete 140-page report. Its exact 1.1 comparisons provide no nominal total or active parameter count. Model self-descriptions in interviews are not engineering specifications.

sources.title: Muse Wonder Model Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 and searched the complete 13-page card. It supplies evaluation methodology and capabilities, with no total or active parameter specification for Muse Spark 1.1.

sources.title: Muse Spark Open Model Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The Meta card explicitly publishes 816B total / 42B active and Mixture-of-Experts Transformer with Perception Encoder for Muse Spark Open. These are developer nominal specifications; application to 1.1 requires the explicit lineage in s13-s17 rather than family resemblance or a tensor census.

sources.title: Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Meta's Glimmer training report describes Glimmer architecture and distillation from a teacher called Muse Spark, without exact 1.1 parameter counts. Glimmer's own size is not transferred to Spark.

sources.title: Muse Spark 1.1 - Meta developer model page
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Exact 1.1 developer page confirms native multimodal perception, computer use and multi-agent workflows, but does not directly state total or active parameter counts. The US-preview description is launch-era wording.

sources.title: Muse Spark Open - Meta developer model page
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The Introducing Muse Spark Open section explicitly describes it as derived from the Muse Spark model released in August, with additional safety post-training for standalone use without system guardrails. s14 identifies that dated model as 1.2; s17 names the release directly.

sources.title: Introducing Muse Code and Muse Spark 1.2
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Dated August 5, 2026. The Muse Spark 1.2 section expressly calls 1.2 a coding-focused update to Muse Spark 1.1 and describes scaling coding-task training compute, training-environment diversity, rejection-sampled harness trajectories and recipe optimizations. It describes no new backbone, pruning, distillation, expert expansion or routing change. This named training-update relationship supports carrying the nominal architecture/count convention backward to 1.1, with the inference labeled.

sources.title: The Multimodal Intelligence of Muse Spark 1.2
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. August 20 post again identifies 1.2 as a coding-focused update to 1.1, ahead of an open-weights release. It describes gains in visual/tool use and audio-visual understanding, not a newly added modality or backbone replacement. Separate experimental robotics/VLA variants are not attributed to the hosted 1.1 model.

sources.title: Muse Spark Is Now an Open-Weights Model
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. October 15 post by the PyTorch Team at Meta publishes 816B total/42B active for Open, says it builds on the August release with additional safety post-training, and links that release to the exact 1.2 launch. This is a developer lineage disclosure, not an unrelated research-team comparison convention.

sources.title: TorchTitan Update: New SOTA Models, Performance at Scale, TitanRL
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. October 21/22 post by the PyTorch Team at Meta explicitly calls the model under its Muse Spark Open heading the MuseSpark 1.2 OSS release. This establishes the named Open-to-1.2 bridge independently of the month alone.

sources.title: Muse Spark 1.3 Evaluation Methodology
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 and searched the complete four-page methodology. It compares 1.3 and 1.2 capabilities and harness settings, without parameter counts or an active-parameter convention for exact 1.1.

sources.title: Introducing Muse Spark Open, The Most Capable US Open-Weight Model to Date
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. October 15 launch directly publishes Open's nominal 816B total and 42B active and identifies additional safety post-training. It does not directly publish 1.1 counts; the 1.1 assessment uses the explicit named-model chain in s13-s17.

sources.title: Cheeky Pint #35: Muse Wonder: Zuckerberg and Wang's $100B AI — transcript
sources.publisher: Cheeky Pint; original interview with Mark Zuckerberg and Alexandr Wang
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. In the October 12 original interview, Zuckerberg explicitly groups Spark versions 1, 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 as having unchanged pre-training and continued reinforcement learning. Wang confirms that Spark and Wonder have different pre-trains. This direct developer testimony strengthens the shared-base lineage for Spark 1.1; it supplies no numeric parameter count itself and does not extend the inference to Wonder.

developer.note: Developed by Meta Superintelligence Labs; Meta is the catalog developer.

family.note: Muse Spark family; muse retains the existing normalized umbrella key.

release_date.note: Public 1.1 launch and API preview on July 9. April 8 was the original Spark release; later provider or regional availability is not this release date.

open_weights.note: 1.1 is the hosted Standard API model. The downloadable Spark Open release has its own name and license; it does not establish a 1.1 weight release.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the exact API model, governed by Meta Model API Terms; not the separate Muse Model License for Spark Open.

parameters_b.note: Nominal 816B inferred from the explicit developer lineage: Spark Open is the 1.2 OSS release with additional safety post-training and a published 816B total; Meta calls 1.2 a coding-focused update to 1.1. In the October 12 original interview, Zuckerberg confirms Spark 1, 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 share unchanged pre-training with continued RL. This strengthens the backward lineage inference without claiming a direct 1.1 count disclosure or exact tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal 42B active inferred through the explicit Spark Open-to-1.2-to-1.1 lineage. Meta publishes 42B active for Open; Zuckerberg confirms unchanged pre-training and continued RL across Spark 1, 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3. No expert or routing change is described. This preserves Meta's nominal active-count convention; it is neither derived from the total nor an exact per-token multimodal count disclosed for 1.1.

architecture.note: MoE inferred through the explicit Spark Open-to-1.2-to-1.1 lineage. The Open card specifies a Mixture-of-Experts Transformer with a Perception Encoder; Zuckerberg confirms unchanged pre-training and continued RL across Spark versions 1 through 1.3. This is a supported shared-base architecture inference, not an independently published exact 1.1 architecture specification. Wang distinguishes Wonder as a different pre-train.

context_window.note: Current documentation explicitly applies this token limit to all three listed Spark versions, including 1.1.

modalities.note: Add documented audio input; PDFs remain a supported input format. Modalities reflect current documented API capability, not only launch examples.

reasoning.note: Dedicated Thinking mode is explicit; later methodology uses xhigh for exact 1.1. This is more than an inference from task performance.

tool_call.note: The exact 1.1 API exposes developer-controlled tool and function calling.

description.value: Meta's proprietary multimodal reasoning model for coding and agentic tasks, with tool and function calling, computer use, and multi-agent orchestration.
description.note: Use exact 1.1 capabilities and remove the inherited generic visual-chain-of-thought phrasing.

patch.notes: Nominal 816B total, 42B active and MoE are inferred from Spark Open's published specifications and Meta's explicit lineage. Open is the 1.2 release with added safety post-training; Zuckerberg confirms Spark 1, 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 share unchanged pre-training and continued RL. These are not direct 1.1 count disclosures. Muse Spark 1.1 is a proprietary hosted model launched July 9, 2026.

summary: October 27 corroboration retains nominal 816B total, 42B active and MoE. The original October 12 Zuckerberg/Wang interview explicitly confirms unchanged pre-training and continued RL across Spark versions 1 through 1.3, strengthening the existing Open-to-1.2-to-1.1 lineage inference. No direct 1.1 numeric disclosure is claimed; Wonder is explicitly a different pre-train. The eleven unrelated assessments are preserved.
